reasons: Both answers meet all rubric items with similar structure. A makes several substantively misleading practical errors: it says the unused balance carries forward only up to 4 years, that the employer route does not work for mortgage interest, and that pre-2009 unused deductions can be topped up. B's errors are mostly wrong citations and historical details, and it gets the DDU acceptance-act rule right, so the practical guidance it gives is somewhat more reliable.

A: Claims the unused deduction balance carries forward only up to 4 years (p. 9 st. 220); in fact it carries forward without a time limit
Claims the employer route does not apply to mortgage interest deduction; it does
Claims a remainder from a pre-2009 purchase can be applied to a new purchase; transfer of remainder applies only when the right arose after 1 Jan 2014
For DDU says the deduction is available after registration of ownership; the acceptance act is sufficient
Lists 6-NDFL as an employee's income certificate and 'налоговые каникулы' among st. 56 forms
B: Cites the purchase and interest deductions as pp. 2 and pp. 3 p. 1 st. 220; they are pp. 3 and pp. 4
Cites p. 1 st. 1055 GK RF for the related-party exclusion; the rule is in p. 5 st. 220 and st. 105.1 NK RF
Says interest deduction before 2009 was limited to 3 million and cites 212-FZ of 29.11.2014; interest was unlimited before 2014 and the law is 212-FZ of 23.07.2013
Cites st. 76 NK RF for the 3-year refund window; the relevant article is st. 78
Dates the employer procedure from 2021; it existed earlier (2021 introduced the simplified procedure)
